concerns.location: tasks.md:T002 [P] tag and 'Execution order' note vs T001
concerns.text: T002 is tagged [P] and the execution-order note says 'T001, T002, T003 are parallelizable', but T002 curates 'neutral prompts from the real stream' and records 'SHA-256 of the original parquet row' as checksums — i.e., it consumes `data/raw/prompts_sample.parquet` produced by T001. This is a hidden producer-before-consumer dependency; either drop [P] from T002 / order it after T001, or state explicitly that T002 streams the dataset independently (and then checksums must be defined against that stream, not T001's parquet).

T008 is tasked to include the robustness hold-out comparison '(d) robustness hold-out (T009)' and to emit `tests.robustness` in report.json, but T009 (which produces the hold-out scores and effect size) is ordered after / parallel with T008. The dependency note acknowledges 'its report entry needs T008's stats module' but the actual data flow is the reverse: T008's report entry needs T009's hold-out RESULTS. As ordered, T008 cannot complete its contract-conformant report.json. Split T008 into stats-module implementation (before T009) and final report generation (after T009), or move report generation to a task after T009.

T009 runs the graph-augmented condition on the hold-out set, which requires parser graphs for hold-out prompts; its stated dependency is only 'after T002'. Add T003 (parser) — and reuse of the T007 augmented runner — to T009's declared dependencies so the execution order is unambiguous.
